answer_1.quote: We prompt GPT-4 to generate CTRL, which states the 'fact' that the answer to Q is T. Step II: generate persuasive misinformation... We prompt GPT-4 (see Appendix B.1 for details) to generate appeals based on the description of appeals and the CTRL as a basis.
answer_1.outputs: persuasive misinformation statements (CTRL) and rhetorical appeals (LO, CR, EM)

answer_2.quote: To evaluate the generated appeals, we introduce two tasks. (1) Textual entailment (NLI) evaluates if the generated appeal supports the corresponding CTRL. (2) Strategy alignment checks if the generated message applies the corresponding persuasive strategy. We conduct these two tasks using GPT-4.

answer_3.quote: We conduct these two tasks using GPT-4... For textual entailment (NLI) evaluation, we use appeals as premises and CTRL to be the hypotheses... For Appeal Alignment Evaluation...

answer_4.quote: We engage five annotators for a formal validation... Each evaluator was responsible for validating the entire dataset... Evaluators are assigned with three tasks: • MCQ: Assessing the expansion... • CTRL: Evaluating the semantic alignment... • Strategy Alignment: Judging whether the generated message applies the persuasive techniques...
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators used binary classification ('yes'/'no') based on specific instructions per task: reasonableness/disjointness for MCQ, semantic alignment for CTRL, and strategy application for appeals (ignoring factual errors).
